criteria.justification: The response clearly and immediately commits to a decision, stating "I would order an immediate rollback of the new release" rather than equivocating.

The candidate explicitly compares the reversibility of the options by stating "Announcements can be walked back; broken trust is harder to repair," showing an understanding of which consequences are easier to undo.

The response directly weighs the ongoing harm of "leaving the core platform degraded for days" and generating hourly support tickets against the momentum cost of walking back a public announcement, which it deems a "temporary PR bruise."
The candidate does not attempt to rush a fast fix, explicitly instructing engineering to "take the necessary several days to build and rigorously test the proper fix" in staging instead.
The response includes a detailed 4-step action plan for what happens after the rollback, including specific messaging for support teams, external customer communications, and a post-mortem.
